neighbours.label: Mild-exclamation interjections 'gee' / 'gosh' (including split 'G'+'ee', 'g'+'osh') at the start of an exclamatory clause
fire: It was a long day at work, and gee, I never expected the meeting to run this late.
You know, gee, Porg, I didn't know you could cook such a fancy dinner.
Achiness, cough and a high fever, but it's not like Gee, I wonder if I have the flu.
My gosh, you really got the whole room cleaned before we even arrived.
Well, gosh, I would like to meet this girl a little better before deciding.
Someone, gee, I can't imagine who, turned off all the lights in the hallway.
Oh gosh, the tickets are still on the kitchen table and the train leaves soon.
I looked at the final bill and said gee whiz, that is far more than I planned.
quiet: Long day at work, and I never expected the meeting to run this late.
Porg, I didn't realize you could cook such a fancy dinner, you know.
Achiness, cough and a high fever make me think that I might have the flu.
Wow, you really got the whole room cleaned before we even arrived.
Honestly, I would like to meet this girl a little better before deciding.
Somebody turned off all the lights in the hallway, and I can't imagine who.
Oh no, the tickets are still on the kitchen table and the train leaves soon.
Looking at the final bill, I said that is far more than I planned.
